title: Volume and surface area
blurb: Find the volume and surface area of boxes, cubes and cylinders, turn cubic centimeters into liters, and see why scaling a solid multiplies its volume so fast.
question: A cylindrical container has a diameter of 10 cm and a height of 12 cm. Using 3.14 for pi and 1 cm³ = 1 mL, how many milliliters does it hold when full?

teach.body: Formally, volume is the amount of three-dimensional space a solid occupies, measured in cubic units (cm³, ft³); surface area is the total area of all its outer faces, measured in square units (cm², ft²). In plain English: volume is how much a box holds, and surface area is how much cardboard or wrapping paper it takes to make or cover it. Read the question for the clue word: fill, hold or capacity means volume; cover, paint or wrap means surface area.

teach.caption: A cube is a box with every edge s: V = s³ and SA = 6s².

head: Solid
Volume

teach.caption: Use 3.14 for π. Cones and pyramids hold exactly one-third of the matching cylinder or prism.

teach.body: For any solid with straight up-and-down sides, find the area of the base and multiply by the height. A box's base is a rectangle (l × w), so V = lwh. A cylinder's base is a circle (πr²), so V = πr²h. A cone or pyramid that comes to a point holds one-third of that. This one idea means you only need to remember the base shapes.

items: Cube with 3 in edges: V = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 in³. SA = 6 × 3 × 3 = 54 in².

teach.h: Surface area of a cylinder: unroll the can
teach.caption: Example: r = 3 cm, h = 10 cm. Circles 2 × 28.26 = 56.52 cm²; label 2 × 3.14 × 3 × 10 = 188.4 cm²; total 244.92 cm².

a 10 cm × 10 cm × 10 cm box holds 1 liter

teach.caption: Cubic units convert by the CUBE of the length factor.

teach.body: Mateo, a nursing applicant, buys a tank 50 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm tall for the clinic waiting room. Volume: 50 × 30 × 40 = 60,000 cm³ = 60,000 mL. In liters: 60,000 ÷ 1,000 = 60 L. He fills it to 3/4 of its height, 30 cm: 50 × 30 × 30 = 45,000 cm³ = 45 L. Check: 3/4 × 60 = 45 L.

teach.h: Scaling a cube: volume grows fastest
teach.caption: Multiply every edge by k and volume multiplies by k³ (double: × 8), surface area by k² (double: × 4).

teach.text: Classic slips: using the diameter as r in πr²h, forgetting the 1/3 for a cone, counting only one circle (or no circles) in a cylinder's surface area, giving the volume when the surface area was asked, and converting cubic units with the linear factor (1 yd³ is 27 ft³, not 3).

items: Volume = base area × height: box lwh, cube s³, cylinder πr²h. Cone and pyramid: × 1/3.
Surface area = sum of all faces: box 2(lw + lh + wh), cube 6s², cylinder 2πr² + 2πrh.
Volume in cubic units; surface area in square units.
1 cm³ = 1 mL; 1,000 cm³ = 1 L; 1 ft³ = 1,728 in³; 1 yd³ = 27 ft³.
Scale lengths by k: area × k², volume × k³.

summary: You can now find the volume and surface area of prisms, cubes and cylinders, use the one-third rule for cones, and convert cubic centimeters to milliliters and liters. You also know that scaling every edge by k multiplies volume by k³.

A.q: A storage box measures 3 ft by 2 ft by 1.5 ft. What is its volume?

whyNot.0: This adds the three dimensions instead of multiplying them.
whyNot.2: This is the surface area, 2(6 + 4.5 + 3) = 27, with the wrong units.
whyNot.3: This multiplies only two of the dimensions (3 × 1.5).

A.q: A cylindrical water tank has a radius of 3 ft and a height of 4 ft. Using 3.14 for π, what is its volume?

whyNot.0: This is the curved side area, 2πrh = 2 × 3.14 × 3 × 4, not the volume.
whyNot.1: This uses the diameter (6 ft) as the radius: 3.14 × 36 × 4.
whyNot.2: This uses r instead of r²: 3.14 × 3 × 4.

A.q: A cube-shaped gift box has edges of 5 in. How much wrapping paper is needed to cover it exactly?
A.why: Covering means surface area. A cube has 6 square faces: SA = 6 × 5 × 5 = 150 in².

whyNot.1: This is the volume (5³ = 125), which measures space inside, not the covering.
whyNot.2: This is the area of a single face; a cube has six.
whyNot.3: This covers only four faces and leaves off the top and bottom.

B.q: A fish tank measures 60 cm by 30 cm by 35 cm. Using 1,000 cm³ = 1 L, what is its capacity in liters?

whyNot.1: This divides by 10,000, one place too far.
whyNot.3: 63,000 is the volume in cm³ (or mL), not liters.

B.q: A closed can has a radius of 2 in and a height of 5 in. Using 3.14 for π, what is its total surface area?

whyNot.0: This counts only the curved label (it also equals the volume) and leaves out both circles.
whyNot.2: This counts only one circle (12.56 + 62.8); a closed can has a top and a bottom.
whyNot.3: This uses the diameter (4 in) as the radius throughout.

B.q: A sandbox 6 ft by 9 ft is to be filled with sand 0.5 ft deep. Sand is sold by the cubic yard. How many cubic yards are needed?

whyNot.0: This divides by 3, the linear factor; cubic yards need 27.
whyNot.1: 27 is the volume in cubic feet; it has not been converted.
whyNot.2: This divides by 9, the square-yard factor.

C.q: A small cube-shaped box holds 125 mL. A second cube-shaped box has edges 3 times as long. How much does the second box hold?
C.why: Scaling every edge by 3 multiplies volume by 3³ = 27. 125 × 27 = 3,375 mL. Check: the small edge is 5 cm (5³ = 125); the large edge is 15 cm, and 15³ = 3,375.

whyNot.1: This multiplies the volume by 3, as if volume scaled like length.
whyNot.2: This multiplies by 3² = 9, the area scale factor.
whyNot.3: This squares the volume (125 × 125) instead of cubing the scale factor.

C.q: A cylindrical container has a diameter of 10 cm and a height of 12 cm. Using 3.14 for π and 1 cm³ = 1 mL, how many milliliters does it hold when full?

whyNot.0: This uses the diameter (10 cm) as the radius: 3.14 × 100 × 12.
whyNot.1: This is the curved surface area, 2 × 3.14 × 5 × 12.
whyNot.3: This applies the cone's 1/3; a cylinder holds the full πr²h.

C.q: A rectangular planter is 80 cm long, 25 cm wide and 30 cm deep. It is filled with soil to 2/3 of its depth. Using 1,000 cm³ = 1 L, how many liters of soil are in the planter?

whyNot.0: This is the volume of the full planter (60,000 cm³).
whyNot.3: This uses 1/3 of the depth (10 cm), the empty part, instead of 2/3.

reteach.title: Think of a stack of paper
reteach.question: A ream of paper is a stack of identical flat sheets. How does stacking sheets explain V = base area × height?

blocks.body: Picture one thin layer of the base shape, like a single sheet of paper. Stack identical layers until the pile reaches the height. The space taken up is one layer's area times the number of layers: base area × height. A stack of rectangles makes a box (lwh); a stack of circles, like coins, makes a cylinder (πr²h). The wrapping around the stack is a different question: that is surface area.

blocks.h: From a flat base to a solid

blocks.text: A pointed solid (cone or pyramid) is not a straight stack: it holds only 1/3 of the stack with the same base and height.

explain.body: V = lwh. To find a missing dimension, divide the volume by the product of the other two: h = V ÷ (l × w).

test.q: A rectangular container has a volume of 360 in³, a length of 12 in and a width of 6 in. What is its height?

whyNot.0: This divides by the length only.
whyNot.1: This divides by the width only.
whyNot.2: This subtracts the length and width from the volume.

explain.body: Cylinder: V = πr²h. A cone with the same base and height holds one-third: V = 1/3 × πr²h.

test.q: A cone-shaped paper cup has a radius of 3 cm and a height of 8 cm. Using 3.14 for π and V = 1/3 × πr²h, what is its volume?

whyNot.1: This forgets the 1/3: that is the matching cylinder.
whyNot.2: This uses r instead of r² (1/3 × 3.14 × 3 × 8).
whyNot.3: This uses the diameter (6 cm) as the radius.

explain.body: A box has three pairs of matching faces: top and bottom (lw), front and back (lh), two ends (wh). SA = 2(lw + lh + wh).

test.q: A gift box is 10 in long, 6 in wide and 4 in tall. How many square inches of paper cover it exactly?

whyNot.0: This is the volume (10 × 6 × 4), not the covering.
whyNot.1: This counts one face from each pair and forgets to double.
whyNot.3: This leaves out the two 6 in × 4 in ends.

explain.body: Cube the length factor: 1 ft³ = 12 × 12 × 12 = 1,728 in³ and 1 yd³ = 27 ft³. In metric, 1 cm³ = 1 mL and 1,000 cm³ = 1 L.

test.q: How many cubic inches are in 2 cubic feet?

whyNot.3: This is only one cubic foot; it forgets to multiply by 2.
